acceptanceCriteria: The TestCALV0053_ReaderExpiredBeforeRetirement cleanup never dereferences a nil cmd.Process, so a failed or pre-start expiry fails only that test instead of panicking the dispatch package run.

The test's expiry no longer depends on a 50ms wall-clock deadline being still open when readerStart runs (for example a controlled clock or an explicit gate), and it passes 50 consecutive runs under -count on darwin at high host load.
body:
Confirmed bug (test defect), observed 2026-10-04 by the #502 claim-delivery session on batch b77ba895 + claude/502-escalations-claim-delivery (tree fb1ea54a), Darwin 25.6.0, go1.27.1, host load average 179-214 from concurrent gate runs.

Failure in a full `go test -count=1 -timeout 30m ./internal/tasks/...`:
- reader_test.go:132 'expired retirement admitted work: context deadline exceeded calls=0'
- then panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference in os.(*Process).signal via cmd.Process.Kill() at reader_test.go:110 (t.Cleanup).

Cause (from source): the test gives stateCommand a 50ms context. Under load the context expires before the reader process starts, so readerStart has set `cmd` but `cmd.Process` is nil; the cleanup guards only `cmd != nil && !collected.Load()` and calls `cmd.Process.Kill()`. The panic aborts the whole internal/tasks/dispatch test binary, hiding every later test result.

Expected: the cleanup guards `cmd.Process != nil`, and the expiry case is driven by an observed event, not a 50ms deadline.
Actual: wall-clock-sensitive assertion plus a nil dereference that crashes the package.

Repro: run `go test -count=1 -run TestCALV0053_ReaderExpiredBeforeRetirement ./internal/tasks/dispatch` under heavy CPU load; it passed in isolation (1.5s) at load ~187.

Related: V1-0724 (PSR store tests sensitive to host load).
title: tests: dispatch TestCALV0053_ReaderExpiredBeforeRetirement panics in cleanup (nil cmd.Process) when its 50ms deadline expires under load
